introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A rigid body is acted on by three forces $\mathbf{F}_1$, $\mathbf{F}_2$ and $\mathbf{F}_3$, where $\mathbf{F}_1 = (14\mathbf{i} + 8\mathbf{j} + 8\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}$, $\mathbf{F}_2 = (9\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} - 12\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}$ and $\mathbf{F}_3 = (24\mathbf{i} + 8\mathbf{j} - 9\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}$.

The force $\mathbf{F}_1$ acts through the point with position vector $(-\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$.

The forces $\mathbf{F}_2$ and $\mathbf{F}_3$ act through the point with position vector $(\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$.

The system is equivalent to a single force $\mathbf{F}$ acting at the point $(1,1,0)$ together with a couple $\mathbf{G}$.
incertitudes: Question 1 : sur le scan, la première composante de F1 s'imprime « 1·4i » avec un point parasite entre le 1 et le 4 ; lue « 14 » (les autres composantes sont entières). Si la valeur réelle était 1,4, F, G et l'équation de la droite changeraient.

Question 1 : le sujet ne précise pas le point de réduction du couple G ; il est calculé comme moment du système autour du point (1, 1, 0), point d'application de F (G est le moment résultant en ce point).

questions.corrige_markdown:
The single force equivalent to the system is the resultant (vector sum) of the three forces:

$$\mathbf{F} = \mathbf{F}_1 + \mathbf{F}_2 + \mathbf{F}_3 = (14+9+24)\mathbf{i} + (8+4+8)\mathbf{j} + (8-12-9)\mathbf{k}$$

$$\mathbf{F} = 47\mathbf{i} + 20\mathbf{j} - 13\mathbf{k}\ \ \mathrm{N}$$

The couple $\mathbf{G}$ is the total moment of the original forces about the point $(1,1,0)$, the point at which $\mathbf{F}$ acts (the moment of $\mathbf{F}$ about that point is zero, so $\mathbf{G}$ is exactly what remains). Let $\mathbf{p} = \mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$ be the position vector of that point.

**Moment of $\mathbf{F}_1$.** Its line passes through $\mathbf{r}_1 = -\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}$, so $\mathbf{r}_1 - \mathbf{p} = -2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}$:

$$\mathbf{M}_1 = (\mathbf{r}_1-\mathbf{p})\times\mathbf{F}_1 = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\-2&1&1\\14&8&8\end{vmatrix}
= \mathbf{i}(8-8) - \mathbf{j}(-16-14) + \mathbf{k}(-16-14)$$

$$\mathbf{M}_1 = 30\mathbf{j} - 30\mathbf{k}\ \ \mathrm{N\,m}$$

**Moment of $\mathbf{F}_2$ and $\mathbf{F}_3$.** Both pass through $\mathbf{r}_2 = \mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}$, so $\mathbf{r}_2-\mathbf{p} = -2\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}$ and their combined force is $\mathbf{F}_2+\mathbf{F}_3 = 33\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j}-21\mathbf{k}$:

$$\mathbf{M}_{23} = (\mathbf{r}_2-\mathbf{p})\times(\mathbf{F}_2+\mathbf{F}_3) = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\0&-2&1\\33&12&-21\end{vmatrix}
= \mathbf{i}(42-12) - \mathbf{j}(0-33) + \mathbf{k}(0+66)$$

$$\mathbf{M}_{23} = 30\mathbf{i}+33\mathbf{j}+66\mathbf{k}\ \ \mathrm{N\,m}$$

**Couple.**

$$\mathbf{G} = \mathbf{M}_1+\mathbf{M}_{23} = 30\mathbf{i}+63\mathbf{j}+36\mathbf{k}\ \ \mathrm{N\,m}$$

*Check:* the moments about the origin sum to $\mathbf{r}_1\times\mathbf{F}_1+\mathbf{r}_2\times(\mathbf{F}_2+\mathbf{F}_3)$, and subtracting $\mathbf{p}\times\mathbf{F}$ gives the same vector $30\mathbf{i}+63\mathbf{j}+36\mathbf{k}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find a Cartesian equation of the line of action of $\mathbf{F}$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The force $\mathbf{F} = 47\mathbf{i}+20\mathbf{j}-13\mathbf{k}$ acts at the point $(1,1,0)$, so its line of action passes through $(1,1,0)$ with direction vector $(47,\,20,\,-13)$. A vector equation is $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+\lambda(47\mathbf{i}+20\mathbf{j}-13\mathbf{k})$; eliminating $\lambda$ gives the Cartesian equation

$$\frac{x-1}{47} = \frac{y-1}{20} = \frac{z}{-13}.$$
